answer: Behavioral correlation fingerprinting clusters accounts by shared timing, phrasing, and transaction quirks, flagging groups whose internal similarity exceeds what independent users show. The rule withholds settlement rights from flagged clusters until each member separates by a shale of distinct behavior across a fixed window. Attackers pay a basalt of sustained per-account divergence: maintaining thousands of genuinely distinct histories costs more than the rewards they farm. A jade of legitimate variance must persist through review, so cheap copy-paste fleets fail while organic users pass.
